message: Thanks. A few quick questions: Which state do you live in? How many people are in your household, and how many children under 18 live with you? Is anyone pregnant or is there a baby under 1? Is anyone 65 or older? Roughly how much does the household earn from work per year before tax? Any Social Security or other income (pensions, unemployment, interest)? Does anyone get health insurance through a job? Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments?
reply: New York. Four of us. I have my son and my daughter. No. I don't really know. I'd have to check. None. I don't really know. Yeah. We have some savings and investments.

message: Understood. A rough guess on income is all I need. Which range is closest for your household's yearly pay before tax: under $20,000, $20,000-$40,000, $40,000-$60,000, $60,000-$80,000, $80,000-$100,000, $100,000-$150,000, or over $150,000? Also, is any child under 5, and roughly how much is in savings and investments (under $5,000, $5,000-$20,000, $20,000-$100,000, over $100,000)?
reply: I'd have to check. No, the kids are older. We have some savings and investments.

summary: NY married couple, 2 school-age kids, own home, healthy, employer insurance, savings. Income unknown. NY CHIP covers kids at high income levels; school meals and refundable CTC depend on income, so a caseworker should verify, along with SNAP, EITC and Medicaid.
